case_name: Mahender Pal and Others v State of Haryana and Others

statutes.act: Act Is An Exception To Section 5A Of The Act
Confers Extraordinary Powers On The Authorities Under Which It Can Dispense With The Normal Procedure Laid Down Under Section 5A Of The Act

To Use This Extraordinary Power As Use Of Such Power Deprives A Land Owner Of His Right In Relation To Immoveable Property To File Objections For The Proposed Acquisition And It Also Dispenses With The Inquiry Under Section 5A Of The Act

holding: The appropriate Government must apply its mind before dispensing with Section 5-A inquiry, and mere existence of urgency or unforeseen emergency under Sections 17(1) and (2) is not sufficient to direct the dispensation of the Section 5-A inquiry.

The Authority must have subjective satisfaction of the need for invoking urgency clause under Section 17 keeping in mind the nature of the public purpose, real urgency that the situation demands and the time factor.
Invoking urgency clause cannot be a substitute or support for the laxity, lethargy or lack of care on the part of the State Administration.
